This key is shared across OCV platform apps (same key found in a834 audit). Enables quota theft, API abuse, or cost attacks against OCV's Google Cloud project.
Hardcoded in AndroidManifest.xml as com.bugsnag.android.API_KEY. Could be used to send fake crash reports or pollute error tracking data.

Hardcoded in classes.dex. This Cognito Identity Pool in us-east-1 can be probed for misconfigured unauthenticated role permissions. If the unauth role is overly permissive, an attacker could gain access to S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, or Pinpoint analytics.
Backend API endpoint exposed in DEX. The /beta stage name suggests a non-production or inadequately hardened endpoint.

report.narrative:
com.ocv.a727 is the Floyd County, Georgia Sheriff's Office community app, built on the OCV (Our Community Voice) platform. At 65 MB across 6 DEX files, it is a large and feature-rich app that bundles an unusually deep surveillance and analytics stack for what is marketed as a community engagement tool.

The app contains 17 distinct tracking and analytics components. The most concerning are:

1. DUAL ANALYTICS PIPELINES: The app runs two independent analytics systems simultaneously â€” Google Firebase Analytics (sending data to Google) and AWS Amazon Pinpoint (sending data to Amazon). This means every user action is potentially reported to two separate corporate data warehouses, doubling the exposure surface for community members who install it.

2. REAL-TIME LOCATION TRACKING (TagAlong): The app includes a feature called 'TagAlong' that uploads real-time GPS coordinates to OCV servers during active sessions, creating a complete movement trail. Combined with the ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION permission, this means the sheriff's office community app can track exactly where users go. Location data is transmitted to api.myocv.com â€” a third-party server controlled by OCV, not by Floyd County.

3. CRIMINAL JUSTICE SURVEILLANCE INTEGRATION: The app integrates directly with Appriss VINE (victim notification / inmate tracking) and OffenderWatch/iCrimeWatch (sex offender registry). While these may serve legitimate public safety purposes, they mean the app knows which inmates users are searching for and monitoring. This data â€” who is watching which inmates â€” is extraordinarily sensitive, especially for families of incarcerated people. The VINE integration connects to vine.prod3.myocv.com, meaning OCV (not Appriss) is intermediating this data.

4. ASSET TRACKING: The AssetTracker feature maintains a local database of tracked items with GPS coordinates, with the ability to share tracked assets. In a law enforcement context, this could be used to track equipment, vehicles, or evidence â€” but the same infrastructure could track anything with a location.

5. ADVERTISING INFRASTRUCTURE: Despite being a government sheriff's office app, it includes Google AdMob SDK with full advertising ID collection, Google ad conversion tracking, and install referrer attribution. The app collects the Google Advertising ID (GAID) â€” a persistent cross-app identifier used for ad targeting â€” and sends ad impression data to Google's ad network. There is no legitimate reason for a sheriff's office app to participate in the advertising ecosystem.

6. HARDCODED SECRETS: A Google API key (AIzaSyASZbllDc_ielyHaBZw120XkaOoeQ11n2Y), a BugSnag API key, and an AWS Cognito Identity Pool ID are all hardcoded and trivially extractable. The Cognito pool ID is particularly concerning â€” if its unauthenticated IAM role is misconfigured, it could expose backend data.

For residents of Floyd County who install this app: your precise location can be tracked in real time, your device identifiers are shared with Google and Amazon, your searches for inmates and sex offenders are routed through a private company's servers, and the app participates in Google's advertising network. All of this data flows to OCV (myocv.com), a private company â€” not to Floyd County government infrastructure. Community members concerned about privacy should carefully consider whether the convenience features justify this level of data collection by a law enforcement-adjacent app.
